_comment: THE EXIT EXECUTOR'S OWN CAPABILITY CONTRACT.
WHY THIS IS NOT deploy/loop_settings.json. Three different roles were
sharing that one file — the trading session, the exit executor and the
newsletter — so every capability any of them needed, all of them got.
They have different authority: a session decides what to hold, the exit
executor places exits somebody else already decided on, and the newsletter
writes prose. Merging them means a capability added for one silently
widens the others, which is how an accidental contract forms. This file is
the exit executor's alone.
TWO PreToolUse HOOKS, AND BOTH BIND. Composition was VERIFIED against the
installed CLI (2.1.241, this box) rather than assumed: every matching hook
runs, and a single `deny` blocks the tool call regardless of which hook
emitted it or how the hooks are ordered — in one matcher block or two. So
the exit-scope gate is strictly ADDITIVE and the general gate keeps every
protection it had:
pretooluse_order_gate.py  GLOBAL SAFETY — kill switch, SHADOW, and (buys
only) live_approved, drawdown, cooldown,
rule-outs, order cap. Unchanged by this work.
pretooluse_exit_scope.py  THIS REQUEST — is the order part of the exact
exit this executor was launched to perform?
⛔ THE ORDER OF THE TWO IS NOT LOAD-BEARING AND MUST NOT BE MADE SO. Never
merge them into one conditional: they answer different questions and a
future change to global policy must not be able to widen per-request
scope, or vice versa.
PERMISSIONS. Read-only broker calls plus the one write call, and Bash
restricted to the exact recording scripts prompts/exit.md runs. `place_
equity_order` is permitted because there is no sell-only variant of it —
SELL-ONLY IS ENFORCED MECHANICALLY BY THE EXIT-SCOPE HOOK, not by this
list. `place_option_order` is absent from the MCP surface entirely
(deploy/exit_mcp.json) and denied here as well.
⛔ THE WRITE ALLOWLIST IS LOAD-BEARING — see OPSLOG 2026-08-20. The RTX
stop executed correctly and was then DENIED permission to write
exit_result.json, which is the only file the monitor reads to learn what
sold; a human had to reconstruct it from the broker by hand. Every file
prompts/exit.md writes is named below. If a step is added to that prompt,
its output file belongs here in the same commit.
⛔ AND THE EXECUTOR MAY NOT WRITE ITS OWN AUTHORIZATION. exit_request.json
and the monitor's control files are denied: a process that could rewrite
the request could grant itself any exit it liked. (The request-id binding
in scripts/market_monitor.py catches that too — the hash would stop
matching — but the two guards are independent on purpose.)
